name: Mavi
label: Mavi 4 Mayor Music
lede: Omavi Minder starts rapping at 14 in Charlotte, makes a debut at Howard that Earl Sweatshirt co-signs, then watches a finished second album die in sample clearance. The record he makes after that, about grief, lands at No. 34 on Pitchfork's 2022 list.

eras.title: Charlotte, and a crew of his own
eras.text: Omavi Minder starts rapping as a freshman and helps found the KILLSWITCH collective. Two mixtapes later, he's still mostly a local secret.

years.src: Rolling Stone · The FADER · Passion of the Weiss · Wikipedia: Mavi
years.h: At 14, Omavi Minder starts rapping and joins KILLSWITCH
years.p: Born in Sumter, South Carolina and raised in North Charlotte, he comes up in the North Carolina crew KILLSWITCH under the name Mavi.
years.xp:
Charlotte felt stunting at first, Mavi has told The FADER, with few peers who matched his lyrics and ear. KILLSWITCH was the fix: a collective of like-minded Charlotte artists that he co-founded. Wikipedia dates his emergence with the group to 2014.

The house he grew up around was musical too. His father was a hip-hop producer and gospel quartet singer who ran a home studio from 2007 to 2011, Mavi told Passion of the Weiss, and he later attended Studio 345, a free production program where he met other Charlotte rappers.

years.p: Mavi's first solo release, put out from Charlotte while he was still a teenager.

years.h: No Roses follows, and KILLSWITCH gets a compilation
years.p: Mavi puts out the No Roses mixtape and appears with the collective on Rosewood Records Presents: Killswitch 2017.

eras.title: Sun talk, and a famous co-sign
eras.text: A debut made at Howard University catches the ears of Earl Sweatshirt and MIKE, and a trip to Los Angeles follows.

years.cap: Mavi around Howard University, Washington DC
years.src: Wikipedia: Let the Sun Talk · DJBooth · The FADER
years.h: A Howard student's debut, Let the Sun Talk, in 32 minutes
years.p: Thirteen tracks, released independently, built on Marvin Gaye's What's Going On and the writing of Toni Morrison.
years.xp:
The title draws on the Five-Percent Nation idea of the sun as knowledge and on Rastafari's "I and I." Mavi told DJBooth that letting the sun talk "is about getting in your 'I and I' bag." Producers include Tairiq, Duckie, Ntvrme, Dkarim, Murky Waters and Nephew Hesh, with Earl Sweatshirt and MIKE credited under aliases.

Sheldon Pearce of Pitchfork gave it 7.8 and wrote that it "lacks clarity and directness at times."

years.h: Earl Sweatshirt puts Mavi on Feet of Clay, then sends him to Alchemist
years.p: Mavi takes a verse on Earl's EP, and Earl connects him with [[The Alchemist|03f3deb7-0419-4bf9-a1e7-511946385717]] in Los Angeles.
years.xp:
On that first LA trip in late 2019, Mavi spent "three or four days" in Alchemist's studio, Rolling Stone reported. He recalls telling him, "Bro, I love to rap." Alchemist later said that unprompted line told him Mavi was "the one."

Mavi's own summary of the stretch: "He was training me up for real."

eras.title: The album that never came out
eras.text: Mavi announces a second album in the year of the uprisings and can't get it out. An EP fills the gap.

years.src: Rolling Stone · Passion of the Weiss
years.h: Shango gets a cover, a tracklist and sweatshirts, but no release
years.p: Sample clearance and other snags stop Mavi's announced second album, and the merch never ships.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone reports Shango was made in the months after the George Floyd and Breonna Taylor protests and reached its final stage. Passion of the Weiss has it recorded in July 2020 with a release date of November 16 that year. Mavi describes it as "very angry, aggressive, volatile, and masculine."

The unsold black Shango sweatshirts are still boxed in his studio. He told Passion of the Weiss it won't come out through "traditional channels," and has called Laughing So Hard, It Hurts a sister album to it.

years.h: End of the Earth keeps his name moving
years.p: The EP lands while Shango sits in the vault. That same year KILLSWITCH returns with Rosewood Records Presents: Killswitch Vol. 2.

eras.title: Laughing so hard, it hurts
eras.text: A record about losing family, made in Charlotte, is the one that finally lands everywhere.

years.h: Nearly every song written in January, two more weeks before delivery
years.p: "I wrote almost all the songs in January, and I added two more like literally weeks before the album was turned in," Mavi told Passion of the Weiss.
years.xp:
He recorded in Charlotte and wrote 10 or so tracks without drums, leaving room to marry his voice to melody. He called the sound "rap as lullaby."

He tried for features from Noname, Earl Sweatshirt and Saul Williams, and none worked out, so he made the record alone: "It's meant for me to do the marathon."

years.src: Album of the Year · BrooklynVegan · Rolling Stone
years.h: Laughing So Hard, It Hurts lands at Pitchfork 8.2
years.p: Self-released, 16 tracks. Paul A. Thompson's Pitchfork review gave it 8.2, and the site later ranked it No. 34 of 2022.
years.xp:
Mavi put the album out himself on Mavi 4 Mayor Music. Lead single Baking Soda was produced by Monte Booker, and the credits include Dylvinci, Wulf Morpheus, Ovrcast, Coffee Black, Jacob Rochester and AMARAH, with Amindi the one guest, on Trip.

Thompson called it "intimate by design but expansive in scope." Mavi has tied the record to grief, including news of an uncle's death that reached him while he was opening for Jack Harlow on the Creme De La Creme tour with Babyface Ray, per Rolling Stone.

years.big: "Laughter is liberation within the black body."
years.src: Passion of the Weiss · Rolling Stone
years.h: The title comes from High John the Conqueror
years.p: Mavi found the folk hero in Zora Neale Hurston's retelling, during what he calls a transformative time of loss, and read laughter as a way through it.
years.xp: High John de Conqueror, in Black folklore, is the figure who survives plantation life by laughing. Mavi told Passion of the Weiss that he came to Hurston's telling while grieving, and has framed the album as the portrait of a person changed by loss who keeps standing.

years.h: Four year-end lists, from Okayplayer No. 9 to Rolling Stone No. 47
years.p: Pitchfork has it at No. 34 and NPR Music at No. 36, per Album of the Year's tally for Laughing So Hard, It Hurts.
years.xp: Album of the Year lists the album at No. 9 at Okayplayer, No. 34 at Pitchfork, No. 36 at NPR Music and No. 47 at Rolling Stone. Its critic score there, from two reviews, is 85: Pitchfork 82 and HipHopDX 88.

years.cap: Mavi at White Oak Music Hall, Houston, spring 2023
years.p: The NPR-distributed interview show talks to him about the album, loss, and keeping a 16-track record to just over 30 minutes.

eras.title: Shadows, then sober
eras.text: A darker record, then a brighter one on a real label, with the first guests of his career.

years.cap: Mavi with family, fans and friends at Archive Coffee Shop after a Charlotte show, c. 2024
years.p: Pitchfork's Dash Lewis called it "among his darkest work, but also his most piercing and inventive," per Album of the Year.
years.xp: Production credits include TwoTone, Beach Noise, Angelo LeRoi and Psymun. Album of the Year lists it as a self-release.

yt: Landgrab feat. Earl Sweatshirt, official video
years.h: The Pilot arrives on Loma Vista, with guests
years.p: Earl Sweatshirt, Smino, MIKE and Kenny Mason appear, which Wikipedia calls his first project with guest features.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports the mixtape documents Mavi's first year of sobriety, with production from Sango, Nephew Hesh, Angelo LeRoi, Asean Bwoy and others. Landgrab, with Earl, came out as a single on May 27, 2025 and was a Pitchfork Best New Track; Potluck, with Smino, followed on June 24.

Pitchfork's Stephen Kearse gave it 7.4, writing that Mavi presents "every version of himself all at once."
